content.text:
Both the dashboard and the alert rule exist, and the rule is enabled.

**Dashboard: "EFF-c482cc9f Web logs overview"** (6 panels, time range 2026-10-01 to 2026-12-31)
- Total requests (count metric)
- Unique client IPs (unique count of `clientip`)
- Average response size (average of `bytes`)
- Requests over time (line, date histogram on `@timestamp`)
- Requests by response code (pie, terms on `response.keyword`)
- Top countries by requests (bar, terms on `geo.dest`)

I set the time range to cover the sample data's span (2026-10-04 to 2026-12-03). Today is 2026-10-12, so the default last-7-days window would have shown only part of the data.

**Alert rule: "EFF-c482cc9f 5xx spike"** (ID `23e88ffd-e2f0-4151-b897-60d58616c2ff`)
- Type: Elasticsearch query, consumer `stackAlerts`, runs every 1m
- Query: `response.keyword` between "500" and "599", over a 5-minute window on `@timestamp`
- Condition: count > 10
- Status: enabled. The alerting health check reports `ok`, with an encryption key configured and a secure connection.

**The rule will not fire on this data.** The sample set has 441 5xx responses in total, all 503s, and the busiest 5-minute window holds only 2 of them. Nothing approaches the threshold of more than 10. The rule works as specified, but if you want to see it trigger, lower the threshold (for example to more than 1) or feed it live traffic that produces more errors.

I did not use the `KIBANA_TEST_API_KEY` variable directly; it isn't set in my shell. All the Kibana work went through the configured Kibana MCP tools, which reached the same instance.
